title: Isolation of Symbiodiniaceae from Coral Eggs Using Centrifugation
author: Sophie SCR Centurino Renton

steps.title: Collect Gamete Bundles
steps.instruction: Collect gamete bundles from hermaphroditic corals as they rise to the surface using cups and pipettes. Label all collections with coral ID and time of spawning.

steps.title: Separate and Wash Gamete Bundles
steps.instruction: Separate eggs from sperm using two bowls of seawater and a filter mesh finer than the target species' egg size.

substeps.instruction: Fill both bowls with seawater and place the filter inside the first bowl, ensuring the mesh side is submerged.
Pour collected bundles into the filter and agitate gently to break up bundles; sperm will pass through into the bowl.
Transfer the filter containing eggs into the second bowl of seawater.
Use running seawater to wash any eggs stuck to the inside of the filter.
Continue agitating and transferring gametes between bowls, refreshing seawater, until bundles are broken and water is no longer cloudy (eggs will form a mono-film on the surface).

steps.title: Transfer Eggs to Falcon Tubes
steps.instruction: Transfer eggs into labeled falcon tubes using a transfer pipette, keeping eggs inside the filter during transfer to minimize surface area.

substeps.instruction: Use the positive buoyancy of eggs to reduce seawater in the pipette before depositing into the tube.
Ensure all tubes have an equal total volume (egg volume does not need to be identical).
Follow recommended egg-to-seawater ratios: 0.8ml eggs to 13ml seawater for 15ml tubes, or 0.5ml eggs to 8ml seawater for 10ml tubes.
Do not overload tubes to avoid lipid production from dead gametes.

steps.title: Initial Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge all falcon tubes in a benchtop centrifuge. Use the maximum speed possible if a high-power centrifuge is unavailable to break egg walls and pellet Symbiodiniaceae cells.

steps.title: Remove Supernatant and Lipids
steps.instruction: Dispose of the seawater and the surface lipid layer ('lipid pancake') into a liquid waste container.

substeps.instruction: Firmly tap the falcon tube on the side of the waste container in one swift motion to dislodge the lipid layer and seawater simultaneously.

steps.title: Optional: Combine Samples
steps.instruction: Combine samples of the same genotype to minimize the number of tubes. Do not combine separated cells with tubes that still contain lipids.

steps.title: Iterative Lipid Removal
steps.instruction: If lipids remain, repeat the separation process until the sample is clean.

substeps.instruction: Top up tubes with seawater to 10mL and pipette mix 3 times.
Perform Round 2 centrifugation: 3000 x g for 20 minutes at 23°C.
Perform Round 3 centrifugation (if necessary): 2500 x g for 12 minutes at 23°C.
Repeat supernatant/lipid removal after each spin.

steps.title: Remove Contact Lipids
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the flaky contact lipid layer directly above the Symbiodiniaceae pellet using one of two techniques:

substeps.instruction: Technique 1: Load a 1ml pipette with seawater, rest the tip on the inside wall just above the pellet, and expel seawater with steady force to lift the lipid layer.
Technique 2: Gently scrape away the lipid layer with a pipette and disposable tips.

steps.title: Resuspend Cells
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cleaned pellet in 1ml of seawater using a 1000ul pipette. Pipette mix until no clumps remain.

steps.title: Prepare Master Culture
steps.instruction: Combine falcon tubes of the same genotype into a 250 mL flask. Label as 'master culture genotype x'.

steps.title: Dilute and Calculate Cell Count
steps.instruction: Dilute the master culture and determine the cell density to calculate the volume needed for the Desired Cell Count (DCC).

substeps.instruction: Top up master cultures with seawater to a known volume (e.g., 100mL) or until they match the reference color chart for workable density.
Determine the Calculated Cell Count (CCC) per 1mL using a haemocytometer (using 10ul of sample, aiming for ~60 cells per grid). Homogenize by pipette mixing 10 times before sub-sampling.
Calculate required volume: Volume = DCC / CCC (e.g., for 5 million cells with a CCC of 587,500 cells/mL, volume = 8.5 mL).

steps.title: Aliquot and Concentrate Samples
steps.instruction: Aliquot the calculated volume from the master culture into tubes based on the required volume.

substeps.instruction: For volumes > 1.5mL: Aliquot into 15mL falcon tubes, centrifuge at 2500 x g for 10 minutes at 23°C, discard supernatant, and resuspend pellet in 1mL seawater.
For volumes < 1.5mL: Aliquot directly into 1.5mL LoBind Eppendorf tubes.
If the sample was resuspended in 1mL seawater (from the >1.5mL path), pipette the cells into the labeled 1.5mL LoBind Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Final Processing and Storage
steps.instruction: Prepare the final aliquots for long-term storage.

substeps.instruction: Label 1.5mL LoBind Eppendorf tubes with genotype and cell quantity.
Centrifuge 1.5mL tubes in a micro-centrifuge at Maximum RCF for 10 minutes at 23°C.
Pour supernatant into liquid waste and carefully pipette any excess water from around the pellets to ensure effective snap-freezing.
Snap-freeze tubes using a Styrofoam raft on a shallow bath of liquid nitrogen.
Transfer samples from the raft to a sample box and store in a -80°C freezer.
